items.title: Sal Gutierrez Interview, 1970-01-15
items.q: We had Fasola, me, and their beautiful, Decamelt, three of us, you know. Decamelt, Fasola, me, on the beautiful. We were glad, see.

ctx.x: Did you ever play underneath Hawaiian skies? You know that, uh... Foozie Rye's about the only one I know around that knows it today. If I hear it, what? Raymond knows it. If she'd turn the machine off, I'd try to sing it. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.
The women there, there were a bunch of characters, they said the Broken Dishes there. The Broken Dishes? That was her name. I had Fazola's applause with Bebe.
You better put down those tails, it's going on in the park, you know. It's alright.

items.title: Sal Gutierrez Interview, 1970-01-15

ctx.x: Nice boy too. He was playing with the rock. Rusty Pérez band. He was a singer in the kind of band. He had a finance company, he made his own Blanche Miller. He went to play the gig in Baton Rouge, you know, and he'd come back, he felt bad. Stopped at the motel, one of the motels up there, died in a heart attack. He was like, no. I was playing with his daddy, see. He was playing with his daddy, see. Oh, you know, talking about this guy, Henry Raymond. He had a picture here, one of those bamboo bamboo bamboo bamboo…
What was it that Lowe used to say, Lowe Pramee, you said, play it pretty for the people?
